literal: Whatever enmity incurred-those-even will-escape; evil-deed-enmity without-ceasing behind going will-destroy.
translation: Those who have incurred even the greatest of enmities may still escape and survive; but the enmity of one's own evil deeds will relentlessly follow and destroy them.
modern: எத்தகைய பகையை அடைந்தவர்களும் தப்பிப் பிழைத்துக் கொள்ள முடியும்; ஆனால் தீய செயல்களால் வரும் பகையானது அழியாமல் பின் தொடர்ந்து சென்று அழித்துவிடும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the inescapable nature of the consequences of evil deeds. A person might manage to survive or escape even the most powerful external enemies they have angered. However, the enmity generated by one's own bad actions (vinaippakai) is different; it does not fade away or perish. It relentlessly pursues the wrongdoer, following them wherever they go, and ultimately brings about their destruction.
